title: AMuLeT: Automated Design-Time Testing of Secure Speculation Countermeasures
problem: Multiple hardware-based Spectre countermeasures have been proposed and then shown to be insecure, yet there is no automated tool to test speculation security guarantees early in the design phase—leaving designers without rapid feedback during hardware prototyping.
motivation: Spectre-class vulnerabilities have persisted despite numerous proposed hardware mitigations because verifying security guarantees is slow, manual, and expert-dependent, delaying both detection of flaws and iteration on fixes.
method: AMuLeT is an automated design-time testing framework for secure speculation countermeasures. It generates targeted micro-architectural test programs (a.k.a. litmus tests) that systematically exercise speculative execution paths across possible speculation windows and covert-channel observability conditions. The tool evaluates candidate countermeasures against these tests using a hardware RTL or ISA-level simulator, reporting which Spectre attack variants the countermeasure fails to block. AMuLeT integrates with rapid prototyping workflows to provide early-stage security feedback.
key_novelty: Automated generation and evaluation of speculation security litmus tests targeting the design phase, enabling rapid iteration on secure speculation countermeasures without manual security analysis.
contributions: AMuLeT: an automated tool for design-time testing of Spectre countermeasures.
A methodology for generating micro-architectural litmus tests covering diverse speculation windows and covert channels.
Demonstration that AMuLeT can identify known insecurities in published Spectre countermeasures.

metrics.other: detection of known insecurities in published Spectre countermeasures

baselines: manual security analysis of published Spectre countermeasures
limitations: Testing coverage is bounded by the generated litmus test set and may miss novel speculation channels not anticipated by the test generator.
primary_theme: automated design-time security testing for speculative execution countermeasures
